newsitem.title: USA: CIA plays down spy impact on business contacts.
newsitem.headline: CIA plays down spy impact on business contacts.

text.p: CIA Director John Deutch said Wednesday he saw no "great jeopardy" to U.S. and foreign business executives who may have been compromised by an alleged CIA double agent charged with spying for Moscow.

But he acknowledged that the arrest last Saturday of Harold Nicholson, a 16-year veteran CIA operative, had had a "pronounced negative effect" on morale at the Central Intelligence Agency, which is still assessing the secrets he gave away.
"I don't think that business is at any great jeopardy here," Deutch told CNN in the latest in a series of joint appearances with FBI Director Louis Freeh to report on the case.
"I think that this will be quite easily managed for U.S. business and other businesses," he said.

According to a Federal Bureau of Investigation affidavit, Nicholson may have given Moscow information about the CIA's so-called "access agents," private citizens such as businessmen who voluntarily share information with the government.
"The identity of these agents is classified, as they could be the target of reprisals if foreign countries were aware of their intelligence gathering activities," the affidavit said.
Deutch predicted that the CIA would continue to enjoy "a good deal of success" in obtaining the voluntary cooperation of U.S. citizens who travel abroad.
Asked whether the Nicholson case had had a "devastating impact on morale" at the CIA, he said: "I think there's no question about it."
